title: Sample 13-11: Sentences with Foot and Caesura Symbols

illustrates.quote: A line break may not occur within a foot, e.g., between the vertical lines.

blocks.features: Opening two lines of Poe's "The Raven" printed once, in the monospaced marked form: vertical-pipe foot marks, double pipe (caesura) after "remember"/"ember", syllables split with hyphens. The plain first writing and the grade-1 second writing seen in the braille are the transcriber's two writings, not print.

lines.text: Ah, dis | -tinct-ly | I re | -mem-ber || it was | in the | bleak De | -cem-ber;
And each | sep-'rate | dy-ing | em-ber || wrought its | ghost u | -pon the | floor.

print.notes: Picture on PDF p.379; foot marks are single vertical pipes, with a double pipe marking a caesura (long pause) after 'remember'.
print.printFeatures: Plain verse lines; vertical-pipe (|) and double vertical-pipe (||) foot/caesura marks in the second writing, with hyphenated syllable breaks.

braille.notes: Verbatim from .txt lines 10945-10955, after stripping a 5-char line-number field (2-digit max line number 11, +3=5) and converting U+2800. Line 1 measures 41 cells (one more than the standard 40) because of a highlighted reference-style symbol at its far right end (see 'uncertain'; the same convention as the end of Sample 13-10's line 1, one cell wider here). Lines 6-11 are the second (uncontracted, grade-1-passage, cell-3-offset) writing; the double foot mark '_\_\' after 'remember'/'ember' represents the caesura, and per rule 13.9.4.d no line break occurs between its two component marks.

uncertain: Line 1 is 41 cells wide (one cell over the standard 40-cell measure used everywhere else in this section), due to a highlighted symbol at its far right; not resolved whether this reflects a genuine 41st-cell convention for this reference mark or a source/extraction quirk. Reproduced verbatim as extracted rather than truncated or guessed.
resolution: Run A and run B independently transcribed this item's braille.lines identically, character-for-character; independently re-verified against the cited source .txt lines (U+2800 blank cells / ASCII-space converted, reference-line-number or box-margin field measured and stripped per this section's own convention) as part of this reconciliation. print.blocks content agreed in substance between both runs (only prose-wording differences in `features`/`notes`, not resolved as errors); run A's wording is kept. See compare-gold-13/differences.md for the file-by-file account. Print description corrected 23 Sep 2026 (see printCorrections).
